relations.myth: Terminus refuses removal for Jupiter’s Capitoline temple
relations.note: Terminus refuses exauguration and remains within Jupiter’s temple, signifying Rome’s immovable boundaries.
relations.source: Cato via Festus; Livy 1.55; Dionysius 3.69; Ovid Fasti 2

relations.note: Dionysius identifies or translates Terminus as Jupiter in his boundary-protecting function.

relations.myth: Both refuse removal from the Capitoline
relations.note: Their joint persistence foretells Rome’s enduring youth and fixed territory.
relations.source: Livy 5.54; Florus 1.1; Augustine City of God 4.23
relations.date: late first century BCE–fifth century CE

relations.myth: Mars, Terminus, and Juventas refuse Jupiter
relations.note: Augustine’s variant adds Mars among the deities refusing to yield their Capitoline shrines.
Varro assigns beginnings to Janus and endings to Terminus in a theological division.
relations.source: Varro via Augustine, City of God 7.7
